_about: LoRC (arXiv:2608.20882v1) on MIDS, 3-class real/pad/deepfake, as a GENERAL member of the fusion. TUNED FOR ACCURACY, not for faithfulness -- configs/lorc_paper.json is the faithful one. Every departure below is either measured on this data or flagged as a prior; run ./run_sweep.sh to select the two knobs that matter.
_encoder_note: The paper's backbone, DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 (hidden 1280). The HF repo is GATED: run ./scripts/fetch_encoder.sh with an approved HF_TOKEN once, and nothing else needs editing -- hidden_size and num_register_tokens are read from its config.json at load time. To run on the local ViT-7B/16 instead: --set encoder=base_models/dinov3-vit7b16-pretrain-lvd1689m (D 1280 -> 4096 makes Eq 6 10x more expensive and r=32 a much tighter bottleneck; see PAPER_NOTES.md).
_preprocess_note: WHOLE IMAGE, NO CROPPING. crop_mode=resize uses every pixel; pad-to-square is deliberately not offered because a constant border feeds near-zero patch residuals into Eq 6's covariance by a class-dependent amount (12% of the frame for deepfake vs 33-37% for real/pad). image_size=384 rests on EVIDENCE FROM A DIFFERENT BACKBONE, and that limit is the point: runs/dino3_resolution_probe.json gives 384 bin-AUC 0.99242 / fake-rec@98 0.9519 against 224's 0.98705 / 0.9331 (512 no better) -- but it was measured on DINOv3-7B with a FROZEN linear probe, not on H+/16 with LoRA fine-tuning. Different backbone, different patch budget, different training method. So 384 is a REASONED DEFAULT, not a settled result for this model; the crop224 arm re-tests 224 vs 384 on H+/16 under the actual recipe, and that is the number to believe. See lorc/data.py for the residual confound that remains (aspect distortion is itself class-correlated).
_compute_note: Measured on one GPU at 384px whole-image: bs16+grad_ckpt = 3.34 GiB / 53.1 img/s; bs32+grad_ckpt = 5.04 GiB / 47.3 img/s; bs16 WITHOUT grad_ckpt = 19.32 GiB / 74.3 img/s. Checkpointing costs 29% throughput to save memory that 96 GiB cards do not need, so it is OFF. batch_size 16 x 4 GPUs = 64 images per micro-step, x grad_accum 4 = 256 per optimizer step -- the paper's 'batch size 64, 4 gradient accumulation steps' read literally. epoch_steps 20000 x 16 x 4 ranks = 1.28M images, i.e. one pass over the 1,257,404-image trainset per epoch; ~1.2 h/epoch on 4 GPUs.

_tuned_for_accuracy.ssl_source=attn_out (CORRECTED): The paper's main text writes Eq 6 over X_res -- BEFORE the bottleneck -- and an earlier version of this code followed it. Supplementary Table 11 ablates the placement and the released model is the AFTER variant: w/o SSL 94.4, SSL Before Low-Rank 95.0, SSL After Low-Rank (LoRC) 96.8. So the text describes the paper's own weaker ablation. The operand is Y (post-W^O, R^{N x D}), not the latent A: Eq 6 states R in R^{BN x D} and Eq 5 gives A in R^{N x r}, so only Y carries the D dimension the loss needs, and Figure 5 routes the N x D tensor into the covariance block.
_tuned_for_accuracy.lora r=16, attention projections only (C: Was r=32 + MLP projections on a 'more capacity' prior. The paper's own sweep contradicts that: SS4.6 states 'For LoRA, rank 16 gives the best result by balancing adaptation capacity and parameter efficiency', with the grid spanning 8/16/32/64. Reverting also recovers the 29% throughput the prior cost (52.4 -> 74.3 img/s/gpu) and drops trainable params 30.3M -> 5.4M. The TARGET SET was never swept by the paper, so attention-vs-attention+MLP stays in run_sweep.sh.
_tuned_for_accuracy.rank=32 (CONFIRMED by the paper's sweep): SS4.6: 'The optimal feature rank for the Low-Rank Attention Block is 32, indicating a suitable trade-off between compression and information preservation', over a grid of 8/16/32/64. It is also the method's inductive bias rather than a capacity dial, and D=1280 here equals the paper's D.
_tuned_for_accuracy.lambda_ss=0.1 (CONFIRMED by the paper's: SS4.6: 'The subspace separation loss improves performance when lambda_SS>0, with the best balanced accuracy at lambda_SS=0.1', over 0/0.05/0.1/0.3/0.5. Still swept here because the optimum was found on VAE-reconstruction data, not faces.
_tuned_for_accuracy.head_input=attn+cls (CORRECTED): Was attn+res+cls. Feeding the raw residual mean to the classifier lets the head route AROUND the rank-32 bottleneck and read nuisance artefacts directly -- which is the mechanism Table 11 says makes pre-bottleneck SSL worse, reintroduced through the head. 'res' and the correct Eq-2 scalar ('eq2') remain available as head_input options for ablation.
_tuned_for_accuracy.head_norm=layernorm (MEASURED, kept): The head concatenates mean(Y) with CLS and their scales differ 11x: L2 norm 0.891 vs 10.092 over 96 real images. A bare Linear is CLS-dominated at init and delivers ~11x weaker gradient to the low-rank attention branch -- the part that carries the method. Not in the paper.
_tuned_for_accuracy.epochs=3: Selection every 1250 steps on es_dev_sel means extra epochs cannot make the SHIPPED checkpoint worse, only the wall clock. At r=16 attention-only this is ~3.4 h on 4 GPUs.
_tuned_for_accuracy.select_metric=fake_rec@real99: The deployed fusion's threshold is fitted at a 99% real-recall floor (tau 0.189821), and this project's finding is that AUC and the operating point disagree while the operating point ships. CAVEAT: a standalone metric is a proxy for what actually matters, which is this member's incremental contribution to the fusion -- see README 'selecting a fusion member'.
_tuned_for_accuracy.lr=1e-4 left at the paper's value: Because run_sweep.sh selects it on es_dev_sel. PE-SPC in this project moved 0.972 -> 0.999 single-member test AUC on learning rate alone.
